title: Aqir Infinite Summons (Alchemist)

body:
# Aqir Infinite Summons (Alchemist)

This is a summon-loop comp built on the Aqir class trait *Infection*. With four different Aqir on board, any Aqir that dies re-hatches a random, higher-level Aqir as long as a same-named friendly piece is still alive — so your board keeps regenerating fresh bodies mid-fight instead of thinning out. Wrap that around two Ogres (Alchemist + Ogre Magi) and the loop becomes an engine: Alchemist eats nearby allies at fight start to become a tanky raid boss, and Ogre Magi multicasts everything the summons do.

The comp's identity is that it does *not* chase three-stars. You deliberately keep multiple 2-star copies of each Aqir (autofuse turned off), because two 2-star copies of the same unit feed the death-and-hatch loop far better than a single 3-star. Its power window is unusually early — you stabilise around round 21 and can chunk players for 15–25% health per fight through the midgame, then scale into the late game with Arc Warden.

## Core Units

| Unit | Cost | Synergies | Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Alchemist | 4 | Goblin, Ogre, Warlock | Carry raid boss; eats allies for HP/damage |
| Ogre Magi | 3 | Mage, Ogre | Multicast on Sand King stuns and Venomancer wards |
| Broodmother | 4 | Aqir, Hunter | Best Aqir to stack — spawns spiders, feeds the chain |
| Sand King | 3 | Aqir, Assassin | Chained stuns, great multicast target |
| Venomancer | 3 | Aqir, Beast, Warlock | Dies into wards that slow enemy attack speed |
| Nyx Assassin | 4 | Aqir, Assassin, Undead | The fourth distinct Aqir to reach the 4-Aqir tier |
| Arc Warden | 5 | Kobold, Shaman | Late-game spike: duplicates same-named pieces and items |

The two Ogre effects do the heavy lifting: Alchemist and Ogre Magi both *eat/sacrifice* lower-level allies at combat start (Ogre trait), which — combined with 4-Aqir — instantly converts your fed pieces into higher-tier Aqir summons. Nyx is the weakest of the four (its re-hatches don't propagate well), but you need it on board to unlock the 4-Aqir tier.

## Items

The build is gated behind one tier-2 item: **Spider Leg**. Put it on a *non-Aqir* piece (Ogre Magi or Alchemist) so that piece's death also hatches an Aqir. Without a Spider Leg, the build does not function — do not force it.

- **Enabler:** Spider Leg (tier 2) on Ogre Magi.
- **Alchemist core:** Blink Dagger and Tranquil Boots almost never leave him — you need the mobility and want him un-stuck. Then Radiance (AoE burn while he face-tanks) and/or Battle Fury for raw damage.
- **Tier 3+ scaling:** everything on Alchemist should scale with his enormous max-HP pool — armor, magic resist, attack speed. Vanguard/Crimson Guard early against physical, a magic-resist cloak against casters.
- **Tech vs Medusa/pure damage:** Scythe of Vyse for an instant hex, and Aeon Disk for a 3.5s invulnerability window to keep Alchemist alive. Do not revive Alchemist (Aegis) — a revived Alchemist loses the Ogre HP bonus.

## Relics

- **Malefic Rapture** — turns the health you lose while lose-streaking into experience.
- **Stolen Vault** — flat gold; take it when you're strong enough to greed.
- **Chiaroscuro Certainty** — after a long win-streak this can upgrade into a legendary-item pick, which is how the guide grabs Scythe of Vyse to answer a three-star Medusa.

## Leveling / Roll Plan

Early game is standard econ: end round 3 either at 10 gold (for interest) or 0 gold, and only commit once you've seen a Spider Leg. Lose-streak for income, ban Humans before rolling (never ban — some of your pieces are the "savages"/Assassins), and push toward level 7–8 before you start looking for Aqir. Turn **autofuse OFF** as soon as you're collecting Aqir so you never accidentally fuse to three-star and break the loop. Buy extra 2-star Sand Kings/Venomancers purely as sacrifice fodder. Wait until round 35 to roll for the three-star Alchemist and take the extra IO / higher max level, unless you're about to die.

## Positioning / Matchup Notes

Place Alchemist front-and-center with sacrificeable Aqir in the four cross-adjacent cells so the Ogre eat triggers on them at fight start. Keep one living copy of each Aqir name at all times or the hatch chain stalls. Two-star Venomancers are better in the front row — when they take damage they spawn attack-speed-slowing wards, whereas an eaten Veno is wasted.

Warriors are the ideal matchup: slow attackers with no burst let Sand King's multicast stun-lock them while Radiance melts the pack (watch for reflect damage from 9-Warrior). The hard counters are three-star Medusa (Stone Gaze + big items) — answer with hex — and any comp that can stun-lock or disarm Alchemist before Aeon Disk saves him.
